_note: Versioned scope manifest for the protected-identifier scanner (#1961, Stage 1).
This file declares rule IDENTIFIERS and their matcher contract. It carries no
rule VALUES: values are supplied at run time through --rules and are never
committed anywhere in this repository. The scanner enumerates its own tree, so
a value committed here would make the tool fail on itself by construction.
Without a rule-value file the scanner reports authority UNAUTHENTICATED and

why_substring_matching: A word boundary needs a word-character transition and _ is a word character,
so a bounded matcher never fires on the token when it is immediately followed
by an underscore -- the shape a public package export takes. Measured against
the pinned oracle tree, bounding suppressed 1 content-addressed false positive
at the cost of 13 genuine occurrences out of 30, the public export among them.
value_source: Not stored. Reconstructible by an authorised reader from the diff of the
commit pinned at oracle.fixed_by, which removed the identifier from this

PID-B1.description: Two names that are individually unremarkable and jointly identifying.
why_co_occurrence: Name 1 alone occurs in 39 tracked files / 91 occurrences at the head this
manifest was written against, including public vessel-registry data, a public
stock-ticker dataset, and an operating-system release codename in a
provisioning script. A bare match on it is mostly non-violations.
No character or line window is used, because any window width would be a
constant fitted to the data it judges. Same-file co-occurrence is structural.
value_source: Not stored. Supplied at run time by the same authority mechanism as PID-A1.

classifications.reason: Resolver-pinned package-index URL path segments and sha256 digests are content-addressed: their bytes are chosen by a hash function, not by an author, so a coincidental match carries no information. Excluded by WHAT THE FIELD IS. The rest of the file is still scanned, and no boundary rule and no whole-file exemption is used to achieve this.

limits._reason: Above the largest tracked blob (64528245 bytes at the head this manifest was written against). An artifact over the limit is an ERROR with a distinct exit code, never a skip.

_sentinel_policy: Exact-line only. A sentinel on any other line does not cover a finding, and there is no file-level form -- the schema cannot represent one.

oracle._what: A leak population this scanner's author did not construct and did not choose. The commit below removed the identifiers; Git preserved the tree immediately before it. Every count is an exact equality against that immutable tree, never a threshold, and never derived from the tree being judged.
oracle._two_sided: Any extra finding fails and any missing finding fails. A subset match is not a pass.

_generated_census_note: Digested by public_surface_snapshot.py so a hand-edit to a generated artifact
moves the snapshot. Deliberately NOT limited to docs/api/**: the last page found
leaking sat outside that census, and a second sat inside it but inside
PAGE_EXCLUSIONS, which the drift gate never regenerates. The scanner's own census
is the complete tracked tree, not this list.
